I traced all 9 tests through the new implementation by hand and they do pass, and the mixed-case / first-last-word logic is a faithful implementation of rules 1–3 in the docstring.

However, there's a real inconsistency: to make `test_subtitle_after_colon` pass, the PR adds an `is_after_colon` branch that capitalizes small words immediately following a word ending in `:` (e.g. "a" -> "A" in "Field: a year..."). This is a new rule that is **not described anywhere in the function's docstring**. The docstring still says a small word is lowercased "unless it is the first or the last word of `text`" — it says nothing about colons. So the code now implements a fourth rule that exists purely to satisfy one test case, and the documented contract no longer matches the actual behavior.

That's a problem beyond style: the docstring is effectively the agreed spec description for editorial/API consumers (and the class of "small word" capitalization is exactly the kind of rule editors will look up). Anyone reading the docstring today would not predict that "notes from the field: a year of remote work" capitalizes "a". Please update the docstring to explicitly document the colon-based capitalization rule (what counts as "after a colon", whether it also applies after other punctuation like `;`, etc.), so the code and its documented spec stay in sync.

Minor/secondary items to consider (not blocking, but worth a look):
- `word[0]` / `word_without_punct[1:]` will raise on an empty string if `text` contains doubled spaces (e.g. `"a  b"` splits into `["a", "", "b"]`). Not covered by tests, but worth a guard or at least a comment about the assumption of single-space-separated non-empty tokens.
- The "after colon" check only looks at whether the immediately preceding *output* word ends with `:`, which happens to work for the given tests but is a bit implicit — a short comment on why the previous colon check is done post-transformation would help future readers.

Given the docstring/code mismatch, I'd like this addressed before merging — either update the docstring to describe the colon rule accurately, or confirm with the editorial team whether that behavior is actually part of the agreed spec (in which case it just needs to be written down).
